assessments.quote: Our data indicate that allowing the operator to choose the "best result" level iteration outline from all generated outlines would likely give the more accurate volume for a given tumor rather than automatically choosing a particular level iteration outline.
assessments.reason: Compares 2D vs 3D iterative watershed for liver tumor volumetrics; touches segmentation accuracy limitations but does not systematically discuss technical bottlenecks or open problems of liver tumor segmentation.

assessments.quote: Image registration and segmentation techniques were applied to enable the visualization of the tumor and the corresponding post-RFA necrosis in the same framework.
assessments.reason: Applies segmentation to RFA coverage assessment, not a discussion of segmentation bottlenecks; no explicit limitations or open problems of liver tumor segmentation.

assessments.quote: This research offers a computer-aided diagnosis system, which uses computed tomography scans to categorize hepatic tumors as benign or malignant.
assessments.reason: Task is benign/malignant classification of liver tumors, not segmentation; no bottleneck discussion.

assessments.quote: In this paper, we focus on an automated computation of optimal needle insertion in computer-assisted surgery with 3D visualization.
assessments.reason: Trajectory planning for RFA needle insertion, not liver tumor segmentation.

assessments.quote: The combination segmentectomy has a certain effect in liver tumor,but it has limitations in some tumors,especially in the tumors with massive adhesion of surrounding tissue.
assessments.reason: Liver tumor CT segmentation method that explicitly notes limitations for tumors with adhesion to surrounding tissue; single small study, not a broad bottleneck analysis.

assessments.quote: Our approach can be extended to other fields of medical segmentation, such as unsupervised domain adaptive segmentation of liver tumors at different CT phases, to facilitate the development of the community.
assessments.reason: Focuses on hepatic vessel segmentation; liver tumor segmentation only mentioned as a possible extension, not analyzed for bottlenecks.

assessments.quote: Segmenting liver tumors from computed tomography (CT) images is a very tricky and challenging task due to many factors such as fuzziness of the liver intensities range, liver pixels intensities values intersection with the neighboring abdomen organs, noise imposed by CT scanner, and variance in tumors and appearances.
assessments.reason: Explicitly enumerates technical difficulties in liver tumor CT segmentation (intensity fuzziness, organ overlap, noise, tumor variability); useful bottleneck evidence though framed as motivation for a CAD system.

assessments.quote: In conclusion, the CNN algorithm can perform accurate and efficient segmentation, with high resolution, providing a more scientific basis for the segmentation of liver tumors in CT images.
assessments.reason: Applies CNN segmentation to liver tumor CT but reports only positive performance; no discussion of bottlenecks, limitations, or open problems.

assessments.quote: However, accurate identification and segmentation of hepatic blood vessels in CT images poses a formidable challenge.
assessments.reason: Discusses challenges of hepatic vessel segmentation, not liver tumor segmentation; tumor relevance only indirect.

assessments.quote: In this paper, we propose a semi-automatic method for liver segmentation of 2D CT scans into three labels denoting healthy, vessel, or tumor tissue based on graph cuts.
assessments.reason: Proposes a semi-automatic graph-cut liver tumor segmentation method; no explicit discussion of technical bottlenecks or open problems.

assessments.reason: Brain tumor review, wrong population and task.
